body: Exactly the same situation. It seems the error popup when there are multiple relations with same column join to different tables with different reference column names. Judging from the sql command generated by typeorm, only one of the reference column names was used, as a global column name, and error popup for other tables don't have that column name.

same here!
This not only sucks BUT it can also cause HAVOC;
I have an example that matches invoices with receipts and joins by id instead of the proper constraint fetching 
different data than it should.
Typeorm has given me  the worst days of my life.

> same here ;;
> 
> @entity
> 
> ```
>  @ManyToOne(() => PublicCampEntity)
>   @JoinColumn([{ name: 'target_id', referencedColumnName: 'contentId' }])
>   public?: PublicCampEntity;
> 
>   @ManyToOne(() => PlaceEntity)
>   @JoinColumn([{ name: 'target_id', referencedColumnName: 'placeId' }])
>   place?: PlaceEntity;
> ```
> 
> Query Error
> 
> ```
>  LEFT JOIN `Camp_Public` `P` ON P.placeId=`B`.`target_id`
> ```
> 
> There is an error looking for placeId rather than contentId.
> 
> **temp solution**
> 
> `queryBuilder.leftJoinAndMapOne('B.public', PublicCampEntity, 'P', 'P.contentId = B.targetId');`
> 
> use leftJoinAndMapOne

Thanks, that solved the issue for me

### Description of change

In `RelationJoinColumnBuilder.collectColumns,` `relationalColumn` is used by reference and `referencedColumn` is overwritten.
Solution: Create a copy of the found `relationalColumn`.

The example is incorrect and leads to the error `QueryFailedError: there is no unique constraint matching given keys for referenced table "typeorm_test_tertiary"`

to fix this you need to add 

```typescript
...
@Entity()
@Unique(["UserID"]) // <-- this
export class TypeormTestTertiary {
...
```

then with [#11400](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/pull/11400#issuecomment-2849034549) query looks like this

```
SELECT 
	...
FROM `typeorm_test_primary` `TypeormTestPrimary` 
	LEFT JOIN `typeorm_test_secondary` `TypeormTestPrimary__TypeormTestPrimary_secondary` 
		ON `TypeormTestPrimary__TypeormTestPrimary_secondary`.`ID`=`TypeormTestPrimary`.`SecondaryID`  
	LEFT JOIN `typeorm_test_tertiary` `TypeormTestPrimary__TypeormTestPrimary_tertiary` 
		ON `TypeormTestPrimary__TypeormTestPrimary_tertiary`.`UserID`=`TypeormTestPrimary`.`SecondaryID`
```
